original_chunk_text: PA Tax Laws (PA Personal Income Tax)  Every Resident, partyear resident
summary: Pennsylvania's Personal Income Tax applies to all residents and part-year residents. Taxpayers are required to report their income and pay taxes accordingly. The tax rate is a flat rate applied to taxable income.

summary: Individuals must file a PA Income Tax Return (PA40) if they earn $1 or more, with residency status determining tax obligations. PA residents are those domiciled in PA or who spend over 183 days in the state, while nonresidents spend no more than 30 days in PA. Special considerations apply for military personnel, college students, and minors regarding domicile status.

summary: The state of domicile taxes income earned by residents, while non-sourced income requires a resident credit from the state of statutory residence. Filing statuses include Single (unmarried or divorced), Married Filing Jointly (even if living apart), and Married Filing Separately (for spouses with different residency statuses). Surviving spouses can file jointly with deceased spouses, and specific residency conditions apply for tax credits.

summary: A joint tax return cannot be filed without permission from both spouses, and specific filing statuses apply for deceased individuals and those who qualify as Head of Household. There are eight classes of income, including compensation, interest, dividends, and gambling winnings. Tax returns are due by April 15, 2025, with a possible extension to October 15, 2025, and penalties accrue for late filings.

summary: Social Security benefits may be subject to federal taxes for individuals aged 65 or older, widows or widowers aged 50 or older, and disabled persons aged 18 or older. Up to 50% of benefits can be taxed for individuals earning $25,000 to $34,000, and 85% for those earning over $34,000; for married couples, the thresholds are $32,000 to $44,000.
